capabilities: Detect attachments that become unlinked while editing a note
Offer deletion of unlinked files in a batch modal
Respect Obsidian trash settings when deleting
Keep a JSONL trace log of every cleanup action
Configure watched folders and permanent delete/keep policies
disambiguation: Not an orphan-file scanner; it only checks attachments of edited notes in watched folders, not vault-wide unused files.
extras: The README explicitly lists out-of-scope cases: orphan-file scanning, inter-note links, and Canvas. The action log is stored at .obsidian/plugins/img-cleanup/data/appendix-log.jsonl and rotates at 1000 entries.
problem: When a note is edited, embedded images can become unreferenced but stay in the vault, and Obsidian has no built-in way to detect and clean up these now-unlinked attachments.
summary: Attachment cleanup tool that detects images and attachments unlinked from a note during editing and offers to send them to the trash.
